data.name: Adil
data.gender_notes: Adil is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Adil is a highly respected Arabic name meaning 'just' or 'fair'. It signifies someone who is upright, principled, and always seeks justice and equality — traits emphasized in Islam and admired globally. The name Adil carries the meaning “Just, Fair, Honest” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Arabic. Parents who choose Adil usually hope their child will grow to embody just, fair, honest and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes moral clarity, divine balance, and truth. An Adil soul strives for fairness in all matters, seeking justice with humility and strength.
data.etymology: Adil belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Just, Fair, Honest.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adil total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Adil
in_english.meaning: Fair, impartial, just, honest, and upright person
in_english.long_meaning: The name Adil carries the meaning of justice and fairness, which are core values of the Islamic faith. It symbolises a person who is fair, impartial, and just in all their dealings. The name Adil is also associated with the concept of Tawhid, or the oneness of God. In Islamic tradition, the name Adil is seen as a reflection of the Prophet Muhammad's own character and conduct, who was known for his fairness and justice. The name Adil is also mentioned in the Quran as a quality that is desired in a ruler, and is seen as a key characteristic of a good leader. In modern times, the name Adil is still used as a symbol of justice and fairness, and is often chosen by parents who want to instill these values in their children.
